Unit.UnitTitle: nixB – A Didactic Laboratory for Software Reproducibility

LearningOutcomes.Paragraph: After studying this course, you should be able to:
LearningOutcomes.LearningOutcome: LO1 (Knowledge): Critically analyze the systemic failure modes of imperative software environments (e.g., Configuration Drift and Dependency Hell).
LO2 (Analysis): Evaluate the "Mental Model" gap in software development using Donella Meadows’ systems thinking.
LO3 (Application): Construct a deterministic, reproducible development environment using Nix flakes and the `uv` Python toolchain.
LO4 (Synthesis): Orchestrate a local infrastructure stack (Bitcoin/Lightning) as version-controlled code.
LO5 (Evaluation): Verify the fidelity of a software reproduction through automated infrastructure testing.

Section.Title: Philosophy and Systems Thinking
Section.Paragraph: This unit explores the philosophy of models and the "Mental Model" gap as defined by Donella Meadows (2009). The didactic goal is to transition the learner from "Technical Tinkering" to "Strategic Orchestration."

MediaContent.Caption: The Philosophy of Models Infographic (Nano Banana)

Section.Title: Hermetic Stacks and Functional Management
Section.Paragraph: Focusing on functional package management and hermetic Python stacks, this unit demonstrates 100% reproducibility through declarative code (flake.nix).

MediaContent.Caption: Nix vs. Imperative Tools Explainer Video (Google Vids)

Section.Title: IaC in Complex Stateful Systems
Section.Paragraph: Applying IaC principles to a complex, stateful technical stack like Bitcoin and Lightning. Students learn to manage system-level dependencies without host-system pollution.

MediaContent.Caption: Anatomy of a Hermetic Stack Blueprint (Diagram Specialist)

Section.Title: Closing the Loop
Section.Paragraph: Automated testing and academic reflection. Validating the reproduction and documenting the process for academic assessment.
